title: Audio Classification — From k-NN on MFCCs to AST and BEATs

questions.question: A classifier receives a short recording and must assign one sound-event label. What task is this?
options: Speaker verification from voice to identity
Audio captioning from sound to a paragraph
Audio classification from sound to a class
Speech synthesis from text to a waveform
questions.explanation: Audio classification maps a recording to a label such as dog, siren, or language; it answers “what class is this sound?” Captioning generates a free-form description, while this task assigns a category from a label set.

questions.question: A 13-coefficient MFCC sequence is summarized by its mean and variance. What is the resulting feature dimension?
options: 39 values
52 values
26 values
13 values
questions.explanation: The summary concatenates one mean and one variance for each of 13 MFCC coefficients, giving 13 + 13 = 26 values. The 52-value option would need four statistics per coefficient; the summarizer computes only mean and variance.

questions.question: Which metric best matches a multi-label audio benchmark such as AudioSet?
options: Word error rate over a transcript
Equal error rate over speaker pairs
Top-one accuracy on one exclusive label
Mean average precision across classes
questions.explanation: AudioSet can mark several sound classes in one clip, so mAP evaluates class-wise ranking across labels rather than one exclusive choice. “Top-one accuracy on one exclusive label” assumes a single class; WER and EER measure transcripts and speaker trials instead.

questions.question: An Audio Spectrogram Transformer receives a log-mel spectrogram. What does it do before its transformer blocks?
options: Runs a DCT on each mel frame to produce MFCC features
Patchifies log-mels, adds position embeddings, then feeds a ViT
Uses raw waveform samples directly as image patch embeddings
Pools frame means into one fixed vector before classification
questions.explanation: AST treats the log-mel matrix like an image: it creates patches, adds position embeddings, and feeds the sequence to a Vision Transformer. The “pool frame means into one fixed vector” option describes a different MFCC baseline, not AST’s positioned patch sequence.

questions.question: You have 600 labeled clips and want a transparent first baseline. What does the lesson recommend?
options: Estimate mAP before building a feature bank
Use a speech decoder to generate class names
Start with k-NN on pooled MFCC features
Train a large transformer from random initialization
questions.explanation: The lesson recommends k-NN on pooled MFCC features as a transparent baseline for a tiny set; 600 clips is below its 1,000-clip guide. A large model adds training cost before the team has established a simple feature baseline on so little labeled data.

questions.question: An imbalanced multi-label evaluation set includes rare sound classes. Which practice best avoids optimistic reporting?
options: Use balanced sampling on the evaluation set
Report macro F1 and recall for each class
Report only overall accuracy for all clips
Drop rare labels before computing the score
questions.explanation: With imbalanced classes, macro F1 and per-class recall expose performance on each category instead of letting frequent classes dominate. Balanced sampling is a training technique; changing evaluation prevalence would no longer measure the target distribution.
